note: Wave status the deck reads. Written by the orchestrator when an agent is launched and when it reports. The deck shows the `asOf` stamp rather than implying live polling — a published page cannot see this session, and pretending otherwise is the same failure as a screen rendering a total it did not compute.
waveNote: Tranche 1 running: four agents on the Golden Path 01 chain — new customer through to paid invoice — because that is the release-blocking path and the one that proves the Mini ERP is a connected transaction rather than sixteen screens that render. Six more product agents wait for tranche 2 rather than launching now: concurrency is bounded by contention, not maximised.

agents.name: Integration & Release
agents.scope: CI pipeline, shared-file arbitration, re-verifying each agent's Definition of Done before anything merges
blocks: every merge to main — no agent merges its own branch
agents.notes: Before this wave opened, the router seam: ten agents were about to append to the same three screen maps in routes/index.tsx, which the dependency graph names as the worst contention point in the repository. Each domain now owns a barrel and composition throws on a double claim rather than silently overwriting. Verified behaviour-preserving — 114 of 402 still rendering, both gates at baseline, 402 smoke routes, 183 app tests.

shared.note: package.json was updated by the orchestrator before launch — vitest, testing-library, jsdom, msw and zod are installed, and the test scripts added — so no agent needs to touch it. That file is the top contention point in the plan. As of W2, screen registration is no longer shared at all: each domain declares its screens in its own barrel under app/src/screens/domains/, and app/src/screens/registry.ts refuses to let two domains claim one name.
